prize_parts.citation: For the development of general palladium-catalysed carbon-nitrogen cross-coupling
For the development of base editing, the chemical conversion of single DNA bases without double-strand cleavage

statement.case_for: Pd-catalysed C-N coupling is the clearest case on the table of a general method whose mechanism is actually understood: oxidative addition, amine binding and reductive elimination were worked out and the ligand logic explains scope. It is used daily in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis, has three decades of independent confirmation, and has two obvious originators who worked in parallel. I pair it with base editing because Liu's work is a new chemical reaction on DNA, an engineered deaminase installing a defined conversion, with a single clear intellectual lead, independent reproduction and clinical use already under way. Together they give two distinct, mature, well-attributed achievements within three names. B007 is a real alternative: the modality is new and the chemistry is sound, but I regard it as the more crowded and less settled case.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation on B029 is overlap with the 2010 cross-coupling prize, which some will read as an extension rather than a new idea, and Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work leaves a priority question. Combining B029 with B052 is also an awkward pairing of synthetic methodology and genome engineering with no shared theme, and base editing sits close to the 2020 CRISPR prize and may be judged biology rather than chemistry. A fair objection is that B007 or B001 would have broader conceptual consequence than a second coupling prize.

responses.point: Buchwald and Hartwig developed the general ligand-enabled catalytic methods independently in the mid-1990s; Kosugi is a precursor and his priority could be raised, but a two-person prize is defensible.
responses.response: I agree with the two-person allocation and I would hold the line on it. Kosugi showed that a tin amide could couple, but the catalytic amination with amine and base, the ligand-controlled mechanism and the scope all came from Buchwald and Hartwig. The citation should say general catalytic C-N coupling so that the distinction is explicit. Where I differ from you is on B028. Photoredox credit is spread over at least seven names, and a three-person cut would leave out Nicewicz, Konig and Melchiorre, so I rank it below B029 on attribution.

responses.point: Base editing turns a biological process into a controlled chemical reaction on DNA, and a Liu, Komor, Gaudelli trio is plausible, though Liu alone may be preferred.
responses.response: I agree that the chemistry is the point, and I value that the adenine editor required evolving a deaminase that acts on DNA. I would still name Liu alone. The prize limit is three, and adding Komor and Gaudelli would crowd out the second part of my configuration. Intellectual leadership of both editors is clearly Liu's, and Nishida and Kondo's independent Target-AID work is a priority complication that a trainee-based trio does not resolve. Your point that the 2020 CRISPR prize requires a distinct citation is right, and I have worded mine around the chemical conversion rather than genome cutting.

responses.point: Induced-proximity degradation is a new drug modality and meets the standard of a game-changer, though no PROTAC is approved and the cereblon-glue and PROTAC strands are partly separate discoveries.
responses.response: I accept that B007 is conceptually the more novel modality, and I ranked it fourth for that reason. My concern is the one you raise yourself: with Crews, Deshaies, Ciulli, Handa, Ito, Gray and Sakamoto all with strong claims, and the glue and PROTAC strands being different mechanisms, any three names will be a contested cut. Absence of an approved degrader also means the clinical consequence is projected, not demonstrated. I would not oppose it as a future prize, but I would not choose it this year over two cases that are cleaner on attribution.

responses.point: Phase separation as an organizing principle of cells is a quantitative physical principle that generalizes widely, and a Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen prize is a plausible configuration.
responses.response: I take the physical-chemistry argument seriously and it is the strongest conceptual case for a cell-biology topic. My reservation is evidentiary, which is the question I always ask: much of the support comes from in vitro droplet assays and overexpression, and the evidence that such condensates form at endogenous concentrations and carry function in vivo is still contested. You acknowledge the condensate versus aggregate debate. Until that is settled I treat B001 as less mature than a method whose products can be isolated and characterised, and I did not place it in my top eight.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will see C-N coupling as a sufficiently distinct achievement from the 2010 cross-coupling prize.
Whether base editing is judged chemistry rather than biology given the 2020 CRISPR prize, and whether prime editing should be part of the framing.
Whether a two-part prize pairing synthetic methodology with genome editing is acceptable to colleagues who prefer a thematically unified prize.
How much weight to place on Kosugi's precedent for B029 and on Nishida and Kondo's Target-AID work for B052.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. I have no known personal or institutional connection to Hartwig, Buchwald, Liu or the other shortlisted candidates; my Stockholm University connection to Secretary Peter Brzezinski is not relevant to these candidates.
